chase_cards.name: Pichu and Pikachu [Bessatsu CoroCoro jumbo insert]
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is a big, physical magazine object tied to a tiny theatrical moment: the Pichu Brothers running through the city with Pikachu, scaled up into a jumbo CoroCoro insert two days before the short reached Japanese theaters.

key_artists.name: Naoyo Kimura
examples: Pichu and Pikachu [Bessatsu CoroCoro jumbo insert]
key_artists.why: Kimura matters because this card asks for warmth and motion rather than combat drama: a jumbo media insert carrying Pikachu and the Pichu Brothers across the movie-short apparatus.

claims.text: The local catalog models the Bessatsu CoroCoro Comic Special August 2000 insert source group as one row containing Pikachu & Pichu at source index 181, with Jumbo as the variant note.

Bulbapedia says this Pichu and Pikachu card was available in Japan as a Jumbo Unnumbered Promotional card on an insert in the August 2000 issue of Bessatsu CoroCoro Comic Special, released on July 6, 2000.
Bulbapedia says the Pikachu & Pichu short debuted in Japanese theaters on July 8, 2000 and was shown with Spell of the Unown: Entei.

Bulbapedia says the top-right border text identifies the card as a Theater version Pocket Monsters 2000 Pichu and Pikachu special jumbo card, and that Jumbo cards cannot be used at official tournaments.

Bulbapedia says the bottom border text identifies the card as a Bessatsu CoroCoro Comic August issue supplement, and that the Bessatsu CoroCoro Special and Pikachu the Movie 2000 logos appear on the card with the CoroCoro dragon mascot in place of an expansion symbol.
Bulbapedia identifies Naoyo Kimura as the illustrator for Pichu and Pikachu, and PokeBoon also lists Naoyo Kimura for the Bessatsu CoroCoro jumbo promo.

Bulbapedia describes Naoyo Kimura as a Pokemon TCG illustrator whose first Japanese cards were Seel, Zapdos, and Graveler from Expansion Sheet Series 2, and whose first English cards were Wizards Black Star Promo Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres released alongside The Power of One.

Bulbapedia says Naoyo Kimura is notable for illustrations in the Neo Series and Southern Islands promotional set, illustrated multiple Pokemon Tales books, and later contributed Pikachu and evolutionary-line artwork to the 2023 Pokemon x Van Gogh collaboration.
Bulbapedia identifies Pichu and Pikachu as a Lightning-type Baby Pokemon card with 30 HP, the Pichu Brothers Pokedex data label, and the An Adventure Together attack.

Bulbapedia says this card is based on the Pikachu short Pikachu and Pichu, that An Adventure Together refers to Pikachu's adventure with the Pichu Brothers, and that the Pokedex entry comes from Pokemon Silver.

As judged collector texture, the Bessatsu CoroCoro Pichu and Pikachu jumbo matters because it turns a theatrical short into a large magazine object, linking CoroCoro distribution, the Johto-era Pichu Brothers, and Naoyo Kimura's soft media-tie-in illustration lane.

narrative.human_title: Bessatsu CoroCoro Pichu and Pikachu: a movie short made big enough for a binder page
narrative.why_it_matters: This is not just a jumbo because it is physically large. It is jumbo because the whole apparatus around it was large: CoroCoro, the summer movie machine, the Pichu Brothers arriving in Johto-era media, and Naoyo Kimura turning that city adventure into a magazine insert. The card was released two days before the short debuted in Japanese theaters, so it feels like a paper doorway into the event.
not_claiming: that every Pikachu and Pichu listing uses this same route

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when a card, listing, slab label, auction description, or agent claim says Pichu and Pikachu, Pikachu & Pichu, Bessatsu CoroCoro, CoroCoro Special August 2000, Jumbo, Pikachu the Movie 2000, Pichu Brothers, Naoyo Kimura, or Japanese unnumbered promo row 181.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat Pichu and Pikachu as a media-tie-in card identity. Establish the Bessatsu CoroCoro August 2000 jumbo insert route before comparing value, rarity, or historical meaning.
steps: Confirm the card is Pichu and Pikachu / ピチューとピカチュウ and that the claimed route is the August 2000 Bessatsu CoroCoro Comic Special insert released July 6, 2000.
Confirm the physical format is Jumbo. Do not collapse this into a normal-size promo, a play-deck card, or a generic Pichu/Pikachu listing.
Look for top-right border text identifying the Theater version Pocket Monsters 2000 Pichu and Pikachu special jumbo card.
Look for bottom border text identifying the Bessatsu CoroCoro Comic August issue supplement.
Check for the Bessatsu CoroCoro Special and Pikachu the Movie 2000 logos, and the CoroCoro dragon mascot in place of an expansion symbol.
Keep the short-film timing legible: the card was released July 6, 2000, while the Pikachu & Pichu short debuted in Japanese theaters on July 8, 2000.

Before spending or trade gating, require seller-controlled photos of the actual jumbo card, including format/scale evidence, top and bottom border text, logo area, front/back, surface, edge/corner condition, and slab label if graded; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.
not_claiming: that Pichu/Pikachu names alone identify the exact print
that a grading label alone resolves the route

narrative.human_title: Pichu and Pikachu: the jumbo doorway into the short
narrative.why_it_matters: This is exactly the kind of object the catalog is meant to protect from flattening. A normal listing might say Pikachu, Pichu, jumbo, promo. The assembly says more: Bessatsu CoroCoro, July 6, 2000, the Pichu Brothers, movie logos, CoroCoro mascot, Naoyo Kimura, and a short that hit Japanese theaters two days later. It is a card, but it is also a little event poster that happens to live in the TCG family.
